label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An estimate based on some knowledge, though not on certain proof.
ex: Without the data, she could only make an educated guess.
note: More reliable than a wild guess, less than a proven fact.

label: READING
def: The ability to produce the intended result; effectiveness.
ex: Researchers tested the efficacy of the new treatment.
note: Usually said of treatments, methods, or policies.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person or thing that perfectly represents a quality or idea.
ex: The old judge was the embodiment of fairness.
note: Related verb: embody, to give a clear form to an idea.

label: READING
def: To decorate cloth by sewing patterns on it with thread.
ex: She embroidered her initials on the handkerchief.
note: Figuratively, to add invented details to a story.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The process of coming into view or into existence.
ex: The report traced the emergence of a new middle class.
note: Related verb: emerge. Not to be confused with emergency.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To send out light, heat, sound, gas, or a signal.
ex: The old factory emitted thick black smoke.
note: Related noun: emission. A source emits; a receiver absorbs.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To use a method, tool, or skill; also, to hire.
ex: The author employs humor to soften a serious message.
note: In reading passages, the sense 'to use' is the common one.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To form a circle around; to surround completely.
ex: A low stone wall encircled the old village.
note: Close in meaning to surround and enclose.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To suffer something difficult patiently; also, to last a long time.
ex: The settlers endured a long, freezing winter.
note: Related adjective: enduring, meaning long-lasting.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make sure a law or rule is obeyed.
ex: The police began to enforce the new speed limit.
note: A law can exist on paper without being enforced.

label: READING
def: To hire someone; also, to take part in or occupy.
ex: The family engaged a tutor for their son.
note: Engaged in means busy with; engaged to means promised in marriage.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To cut words or designs into a hard surface.
ex: The jeweler engraved the date inside the ring.
note: Figuratively, engraved in memory means impossible to forget.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To improve the quality, value, or strength of something.
ex: Good lighting can enhance the colors of a painting.
note: Enhances something already present; does not create it.

label: READING
def: Having the right to have or do something.
ex: Every citizen is entitled to a fair trial.
note: Also means 'having the title': a book entitled Hope.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Something that exists as a separate, independent unit.
ex: The company became a separate legal entity.
note: A formal, general word for a thing, body, or organization.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A scientist who studies insects.
ex: The entomologist spent years studying ants in the desert.
note: Pairs in analogies as expert : subject (entomologist : insects).

label: READING
def: To list things one by one.
ex: The contract enumerates the duties of each partner.
note: Stresses counting off items, not explaining them.

label: READING
def: A state of balance between opposing forces or influences.
ex: The market reached equilibrium when supply matched demand.
note: Can also mean calm mental balance.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A sudden, violent outburst, especially of a volcano.
ex: The eruption buried the town under ash.
note: Figuratively, an eruption of anger or violence.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The accepted rules of polite behavior in a society or group.
ex: Court etiquette required guests to bow to the queen.
note: Rules of form, not of law.

label: READING
def: To empty a place, or remove people from a dangerous place.
ex: Firefighters evacuated everyone from the burning building within minutes.
note: Related noun: evacuation.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To judge the value, quality, or importance of something.
ex: Teachers evaluate each project according to clear criteria.
note: Evaluation involves judgment, not just description.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Having high rank or great honor; also, very joyful.
ex: She held an exalted position at the royal court.
note: Verb: exalt, to praise highly. Do not confuse with exulted, meaning rejoiced.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: So good that it serves as an example for others.
ex: Her exemplary conduct earned her a public award.
note: An exemplary figure is a model to imitate.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To come to the end of a period of validity.
ex: His passport expired a week before the trip.
note: Formally, it can also mean to die.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To leave uncovered or unprotected; also, to reveal a hidden truth.
ex: The article exposed corruption in the city council.
note: Related noun: exposure, as in exposure to sunlight.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: No longer existing, especially of a species that has died out.
ex: The dodo became extinct in the seventeenth century.
note: A mass extinction wipes out many species at once.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The holding of extreme political or religious views.
ex: The speech warned against extremism of every kind.
note: Contrast with moderation.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A short story, often with animals, that teaches a moral lesson.
ex: In the fable, the patient tortoise beats the hare.
note: A fable carries a moral; a myth explains origins or beliefs.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To gradually lose color, brightness, strength, or importance.
ex: The painted sign had faded in the sun.
note: Figuratively, fame or hope can fade: her popularity slowly faded.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Weak and hard to see, hear, or smell.
ex: A faint glow appeared on the horizon before dawn.
note: As a verb, to faint is to lose consciousness briefly.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A severe, widespread shortage of food.
ex: Thousands fled the region during the famine.
note: Drought (lack of rain) often causes famine (lack of food).

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To understand something difficult after much thought.
ex: She could not fathom why he had left.
note: Usually used in the negative: could not fathom.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make soil richer; also, to start reproduction in an egg or plant.
ex: Farmers fertilize the fields before planting.
note: Related noun: fertilizer.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Invented by the imagination; not real.
ex: Sherlock Holmes is a fictional detective.
note: Fictional means invented; fictitious often means false.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A strip of cleared land that stops a fire from spreading.
ex: The rangers cut a firebreak to protect the village.
note: Pairs as protection : danger, like a levee : flood.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Suitable or appropriate for the situation.
ex: The award was a fitting end to her career.
note: As a noun, a fitting is a trying-on of clothes or a small part.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: In a firm, direct way that allows no discussion.
ex: The minister flatly refused to answer the question.
note: Flatly refused means refused completely, not politely.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To grow or develop successfully and vigorously.
ex: The arts flourished during the long period of peace.
note: Contrast with decline or wither.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A young horse.
ex: The foal stayed close to its mother.
note: Young : adult pairs, like calf : cow or lamb : sheep.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A fake copy made to deceive; also, the crime of making one.
ex: The painting was exposed as a clever forgery.
note: Related verb: forge, which can also mean to form or create.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To create or express an idea or plan carefully.
ex: The committee formulated a new policy on housing.
note: Related noun: formulation.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To turn into a fossil; figuratively, to become rigid and outdated.
ex: The bones had fossilized over millions of years.
note: A fossilized idea no longer changes with the times.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Easily broken or damaged.
ex: Pack the fragile vases in soft paper.
note: Contrast with sturdy or robust.

label: READING
def: To break into small pieces; as a noun, a broken piece.
ex: The ancient scroll had fragmented into tiny pieces.
note: A fragmented society is divided into separate groups.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Honest and direct, even when the truth is unwelcome.
ex: She gave me a frank opinion of my essay.
note: Frankness can seem rude but is not intended to hurt.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: The resistance when surfaces rub; figuratively, conflict between people.
ex: Oil reduces friction between the moving parts.
note: Friction between colleagues means tension or disagreement.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: From the very beginning.
ex: The plan was doomed from the outset.
note: Similar to from the start.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A broad statement based on limited cases.
ex: It is risky to make generalizations from a single example.
note: A sweeping generalization ignores important exceptions.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A scientist who studies rocks and the earth's structure.
ex: The geologist examined layers of rock in the canyon.
note: Expert : subject pairs, like geologist : rocks.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A huge, slow-moving mass of ice.
ex: The glacier has retreated several kilometers this century.
note: Glacial also means extremely slow or cold.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A faint, unsteady light; also, a small sign of something.
ex: There was a glimmer of hope in her voice.
note: Weaker than a glow or a blaze.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To praise highly, often more than is deserved.
ex: The film was criticized for glorifying violence.
note: Often suggests unjustified praise.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Close-fitting glasses that protect the eyes.
ex: The welder lowered his goggles before starting work.
note: Protective gear : body part, like helmet : head.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To give or allow something formally; as a noun, money given for a purpose.
ex: The university granted her permission to study abroad.
note: Take for granted means assume without question.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Very serious and worrying.
ex: The doctor said the situation was grave.
note: As a noun, a place of burial.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A long, narrow cut in a surface.
ex: The needle followed the groove in the record.
note: A groove guides movement along a fixed path.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A railing that prevents people or vehicles from falling.
ex: The car struck the guardrail but stayed on the road.
note: Protection : danger pairs in analogies.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The passage from the mouth to the stomach; the throat.
ex: The heron swallowed the fish whole, straight down its gullet.
note: An informal word for the esophagus.

label: READING
def: The process of becoming used to something through repetition.
ex: Through habituation, the birds stopped fearing the scarecrow.
note: Related verb: habituate.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A sheltered place for ships; as a verb, to keep a feeling or hide someone.
ex: She harbored a secret dislike for her neighbor.
note: Harbor is to ship as garage is to car.

label: READING
def: A danger or risk.
ex: Wet floors are a common hazard in kitchens.
note: Hazardous means dangerous.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who believes pleasure is the most important goal in life.
ex: The hedonist spent his fortune on fine food and travel.
note: Contrast with an ascetic, who avoids pleasure.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who will inherit property, rank, or a title.
ex: The prince was the heir to the throne.
note: Pronounced like air; the h is silent.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Understanding a situation only after it has happened.
ex: In hindsight, we should have left earlier.
note: Contrast with foresight, which comes beforehand.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: The dry outer covering of some seeds or fruits.
ex: They removed the husks before cooking the corn.
note: Covering : contents, like shell : egg.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A religious song of praise.
ex: The congregation stood to sing a hymn.
note: A type of song, as a sonnet is a type of poem.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To picture something as better or more perfect than it is.
ex: Many adults idealize their childhood and forget its difficulties.
note: An idealized image ignores flaws.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The state of being inactive or avoiding work.
ex: Months of idleness left him restless.
note: Contrast with industriousness.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Lack of knowledge or information.
ex: His rude remark came from ignorance, not malice.
note: Ignorance is not knowing; ignoring is choosing not to notice.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A false idea or a deceptive appearance.
ex: The mirrors created the illusion of a larger room.
note: Do not confuse with allusion, an indirect reference.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Descriptive language that creates pictures in the reader's mind.
ex: The poem's imagery of the sea is striking.
note: Also refers to visual images in general.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To put completely into a liquid; to involve oneself deeply.
ex: She immersed herself in her studies.
note: Noun: immersion; language immersion means learning by living in the language.

label: READING
def: Too slight or gradual to be noticed.
ex: The change in the light was almost imperceptible.
note: Contrast with conspicuous.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To put a plan or decision into action.
ex: The school will implement the new schedule next month.
note: As a noun, an implement is a tool.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Something suggested without being stated directly; a likely consequence.
ex: The implication of his remark was that we had failed.
note: Related verb: imply. The speaker implies; the listener infers.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To force a rule, burden, or penalty on someone.
ex: The government imposed strict limitations on imports.
note: To impose on someone also means to take unfair advantage.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A mark made by pressing; a lasting effect.
ex: The boot left a deep imprint in the mud.
note: Figuratively, an experience can leave an imprint on memory.

label: READING
def: Moving at the same pace as; in agreement with.
ex: Wages have not risen in step with prices.
note: Out of step with means not matching or not in agreement.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Not enough or not good enough for a purpose.
ex: The supplies proved inadequate for the long journey.
note: Contrast with adequate.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Not alive; without life or movement.
ex: A stone is an inanimate object.
note: Contrast with animate, meaning living.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Present from birth rather than learned.
ex: She had an inborn talent for music.
note: Synonym: innate. Contrast with acquired.

label: READING
def: To slope or tilt; also, to tend toward an attitude.
ex: The road inclines steeply toward the hilltop.
note: Inclined to means likely or tending to.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Including everything or everyone; not excluding anyone.
ex: The club aims to be inclusive of all ages.
note: Also, counting the endpoints: Monday to Friday inclusive.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: So similar that the difference cannot be seen.
ex: The copy was indistinguishable from the original.
note: Related verb: distinguish, to tell apart.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Hard-working and diligent.
ex: The industrious student finished her project early.
note: Not the same as industrial, which relates to industry.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Early childhood; also, the earliest stage of development.
ex: Space tourism is still in its infancy.
note: Figurative use is common in reading passages.

label: READING
def: Lower in quality, rank, or value.
ex: The cheap fabric was clearly inferior.
note: Inferior to, not inferior than. Contrast with superior.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Without limits or end.
ex: Some scientists believe the universe is infinite, with no edge at all.
note: Informally, extremely great: infinite patience.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The basic systems a society needs, such as roads and power.
ex: The storm damaged the region's infrastructure.
note: Includes transport, water, energy, and communications.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Cleverness and originality in solving problems.
ex: The prisoners escaped through sheer ingenuity.
note: Related adjective: ingenious. Do not confuse with ingenuous, meaning innocent.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Firmly fixed and hard to change.
ex: Such habits are deeply ingrained in our culture.
note: Close in meaning to entrenched.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To slow down, restrict, or prevent a process or action.
ex: Cold temperatures inhibit the growth of bacteria.
note: Related noun: inhibition, also meaning shyness.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Existing from birth; natural rather than learned.
ex: Some linguists believe language ability is innate.
note: Synonym: inborn. Contrast with acquired.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To write or carve words on a surface.
ex: Their names were inscribed on the monument.
note: Related noun: inscription.

label: READING
def: Unaware of or unaffected by something.
ex: He seemed insensible to the cold.
note: Not the same as insensitive, meaning unkind.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Unable to be separated; always together.
ex: The two friends were inseparable as children.
note: Contrast with separable.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A deep and clear understanding of something.
ex: The book offers insight into life in ancient Rome.
note: Insightful means showing such understanding.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A careful examination to check condition or quality.
ex: The building failed its safety inspection.
note: Related verb: inspect. An inspector carries out inspections.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The amount of something taken in, especially food or air.
ex: Doctors recommend reducing your daily intake of salt.
note: Also, the people admitted at one time: this year's intake.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To become or make stronger or more extreme.
ex: The storm intensified as it approached the coast.
note: Related noun: intensity.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To stop or catch something on its way somewhere.
ex: Guards intercepted the letter before it arrived.
note: In math, an intercept is where a line crosses an axis.

label: READING
def: Able to be exchanged for each other without difference.
ex: The two words are not always interchangeable.
note: Interchangeable parts fit any machine of the same model.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Relating to relationships and communication between people.
ex: The job requires strong interpersonal skills.
note: Contrast with intrapersonal, within one person.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To frighten someone, especially to make them obey.
ex: The bully tried to intimidate the younger children.
note: Being intimidated means feeling frightened or overawed.

label: READING
def: To call upon something as a reason, authority, or explanation.
ex: The lawyer invoked an old law to support her case.
note: Can also mean to call upon a god for help.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Done without conscious control or choice.
ex: A sneeze is an involuntary reaction.
note: Contrast with voluntary or deliberate.

label: READING
def: In a way that can never be recovered or put right.
ex: The files were irretrievably lost in the fire.
note: Close in meaning to irreversibly.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Impossible to undo or change back.
ex: The damage to the forest was irreversible.
note: Contrast with reversible or temporary.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Supplying land with water through channels or pipes.
ex: Irrigation turned the desert into farmland.
note: Remedy : problem pairs, like irrigation : drought.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A member of a jury in a court case.
ex: Each juror listened carefully to the witnesses.
note: Member : group, like juror : jury.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A young person or animal; also, childish.
ex: The court handles cases involving juveniles.
note: As an adjective, can criticize immature behavior.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Present but hidden or not yet developed.
ex: The crisis revealed his latent talent for leadership.
note: Contrast with manifest or evident.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A false written statement that damages someone's reputation.
ex: The newspaper was sued for libel.
note: Libel is written; slander is spoken.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Officially permitted to do or own something.
ex: Only a licensed electrician may do this work.
note: Related noun: license, an official permit.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A metal rod that safely directs lightning into the ground.
ex: A lightning rod protected the church tower.
note: Figuratively, a person who attracts criticism.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A group of young animals born at the same time; also, trash.
ex: The cat gave birth to a litter of five kittens.
note: Group : member, like litter : kitten.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Very tall; also, noble or grand in ideas.
ex: The speech was full of lofty ideals.
note: Can also mean proud and superior.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Believed or kept for a long time.
ex: New evidence challenged a long-held theory.
note: Often paired with belief, view, or assumption.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Applying oil or grease to reduce friction.
ex: The engine failed from a lack of lubrication.
note: Remedy : problem pairs, like lubrication : friction.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Relating to the sea.
ex: Marine biologists study life in the ocean.
note: A marine is also a soldier serving on ships.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A process or system by which something works or happens.
ex: Scientists studied the mechanism of memory.
note: Also, the moving parts of a machine.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who buys and sells goods, especially in trade.
ex: The merchants brought silk from the East.
note: Related noun: merchandise, the goods for sale.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A very large and important city.
ex: Tokyo is a vast metropolis of millions of people.
note: Related adjective: metropolitan.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To move from one region to another, often seasonally.
ex: The birds migrate south every autumn.
note: Emigrate means leaving a country; migrate is more general.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Extremely small.
ex: A minuscule error ruined the whole experiment.
note: Often misspelled miniscule. A stronger degree of small.

label: READING
def: Based on a mistaken idea or poor judgment.
ex: The plan was misconceived from the beginning.
note: Related noun: misconception.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Improper or unacceptable behavior, especially by a professional.
ex: The officer was dismissed for misconduct.
note: Stronger than a mistake; a breach of rules.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A person who hoards money and hates spending it.
ex: The miser lived in poverty despite his wealth.
note: A miser is extreme; a frugal person is sensibly careful.

label: READING
def: A change made to something, usually to improve it.
ex: The design needed only minor modification.
note: Related verb: modify.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A system of government in which a king or queen rules.
ex: France was a monarchy before the revolution.
note: Adjective: monarchical. Contrast with republic.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A picture made from small pieces of stone, glass, or tile.
ex: The floor was decorated with a Roman mosaic.
note: Figuratively, a mixture of many different parts.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A reason for doing something.
ex: The police could find no motive for the crime.
note: Related noun: motivation.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Dark and dirty; also, unclear or suspicious.
ex: The details of the deal remain murky.
note: Contrast with clear or transparent.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A soft, low, continuous sound, especially of voices.
ex: A murmur of approval spread through the crowd.
note: A weaker degree of sound, as a whisper is to a shout.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A traditional story explaining beliefs; also, a widely held false belief.
ex: It is a myth that goldfish have short memories.
note: Related noun: mythology.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A person who plans and directs the route of a ship or plane.
ex: The navigator plotted a course using the stars.
note: Role : task pairs, like navigator : route.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To cancel the effect of something; to deny.
ex: One mistake can negate months of hard work.
note: Related noun: negation.

label: READING
def: To reach agreement through discussion; also, to get past an obstacle.
ex: The truck slowly negotiated the narrow mountain road.
note: The travel sense often surprises readers.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The highest social class; also, the quality of being noble.
ex: Members of the nobility owned most of the land.
note: Moral nobility means honesty and generosity.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: New and original; as a noun, a long fictional book.
ex: The scientist proposed a novel solution to the problem.
note: Novel (new) differs from novice (beginner).

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A beginner with little experience.
ex: The course is designed for novices.
note: Contrast with expert or veteran.
